notes.process_name: The process preset really is named '@BBL X1C' for a P1S. The P1S machine profile's own default_print_profile says so, and the process's compatible_printers lists 'Bambu Lab P1S 0.4 nozzle'. Do not 'fix' it to '@BBL P1S' - that file does not exist and the slice fails with return_code -17.
notes.env_overrides: THREEDP_SLICER overrides the executable; THREEDP_SLICER_PROFILES overrides profile_root. Both raise when set to something that is not there, rather than falling back.
notes.orcaslicer: OrcaSlicer is a Bambu Studio fork and shares the CLI surface and the '; FEATURE:' G-code markers, so it sits in the candidate list. It is NOT installed on this machine and has not been exercised.
notes.bed_type: The CLI writes `; curr_bed_type = Cool Plate` unless told otherwise, because default_bed_type lives in the printer-MODEL json (Bambu Lab P1S.json) and not in the machine-PRESET chain --load-settings walks. The P1S ships a textured PEI plate, so the sliced first-layer bed temperature was the cool-plate one (35 C) instead of the textured one (55 C). Measured 2026-08-02 (S23). bed_type:'auto' over MQTT does NOT fix this - the temperature is baked into the G-code long before MQTT sees it.
notes.frame_materials: PA-CF and TPU are the fpv frame's materials (seanrobertwright/fpv #5): Bambu PAHT-CF (filament_id GFN04, filament_type PA-CF, density 1.06) and Bambu TPU 95A (GFU01, filament_type TPU, density 1.22). The keys are the filament_type the AMS reports as tray_type, because ams_mapping and printer.reconcile_ams match on that string; neither spool has been loaded yet, so the tray_type spelling is from Bambu's filament profiles, not from telemetry. Bambu ships no '@BBL P1S 0.4 nozzle' file for either; the '@BBL X1C' presets list 'Bambu Lab P1S 0.4 nozzle' in compatible_printers. Read from github.com/bambulab/BambuStudio resources/profiles/BBL/filament on 2026-10-07; not yet flattened on this machine because no Bambu Studio install was found here that day. Data sheets: Bambu PAHT-CF TDS V3.0 (wiki.bambulab.com/filament-acc/asacf-pahtcf/65f1b18a6d6142d794a1a6a00f1496ef.pdf): nozzle 260-290 C, bed 80-100 C, chamber 45-60 C, dry 80 C 8-12 h, density 1.06. Bambu TPU 95A TDS V2.0 (cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0584/7236/6216/files/Bambu_TPU_95A_Technical_Data_Sheet.pdf): nozzle 220-240 C, bed 30-35 C, fan 100%, dry 70 C 8 h, speed < 80 mm/s, density 1.20 where the slicer profile says 1.22; the profile's figure is what the slice report will use. TPU is not AMS-compatible (Bambu filament guide: too soft for the feed channel) and runs from the external spool.
notes.material_process_overrides: Process settings keyed by material, merged after preset_overrides.process for that material only. PA-CF is the frame's structural material and its parts are modelled hollow with explicit walls (fpv ADR 0002), so anything modelled solid must print solid: sparse_infill_density 100%. Pattern alignedrectilinear with infill_direction 0 lays every internal solid line along plate X, which is the arm axis when arms are placed along X: in BambuStudio's Fill code every fill takes infill_direction as its base angle and FillBase::_layer_angle alternates it by 90 deg per layer, while FillAlignedRectilinear overrides _layer_angle to 0 (src/libslic3r/Fill/FillRectilinear.hpp). The top/bottom shell layers still alternate, so a skin is part along, part across. UNVERIFIED on G-code: no slicer was installed on this machine on 2026-10-07; check the preview when one is.
